questions.question: Which of the following represents pure capacitive reactance of 100 ohms in rectangular notation?
How are impedances described in polar coordinates?
Which of the following represents a pure inductive reactance in polar coordinates?
What type of Y-axis scale is most often used for graphs of circuit frequency response?
What kind of diagram is used to show the phase relationship between impedances at a given frequency?
What does the impedance 50 - j25 ohms represent?

choices.A: 50 ohms resistance in series with 25 ohms inductive reactance
choices.B: 50 ohms resistance in series with 25 ohms capacitive reactance
choices.C: 25 ohms resistance in series with 50 ohms inductive reactance
choices.D: 25 ohms resistance in series with 50 ohms capacitive reactance

questions.answer: 50 ohms resistance in series with 25 ohms capacitive reactance

questions.question: Where is the impedance of a pure resistance plotted on rectangular coordinates?

choices.B: On a line through the origin, slanted at 45 degrees
choices.C: On a horizontal line, offset vertically above the horizontal axis

questions.question: What coordinate system is often used to display the phase angle of a circuit containing resistance, inductive, and/or capacitive reactance?
When using rectangular coordinates to graph the impedance of a circuit, what do the axes represent?

choices.A: The X axis represents the resistive component, and the Y axis represents the reactive component
choices.B: The X axis represents the reactive component, and the Y axis represents the resistive component
choices.C: The X axis represents the phase angle, and the Y axis represents the magnitude
choices.D: The X axis represents the magnitude, and the Y axis represents the phase angle

questions.answer: The X axis represents the resistive component, and the Y axis represents the reactive component
